personal_information.headline: MASTER BELLFOUNDER / CAMPANOLOGIST / TOWER RESTORATION CONSULTANT

summary: I did not choose bells. My grandfather cast them, my father turned them, and by the time I was seventeen I understood that I would spend my life listening for the note hidden inside raw bronze. What follows is the record of that listening.

work_experience.employer: My grandfather's small casting workshop (a village outside)
details: A village outside Loughborough, weekends and school holidays, 1991–1999. My grandfather ran a much smaller casting operation than either employer listed above, largely repair and small agricultural bell work, and I spent most weekends from age eleven sweeping the yard, mixing loam for moulds, and eventually being allowed to help pour small bells under close supervision. This is not formal employment and predates my apprenticeship by nearly a decade, but it is, in every way that matters, where this career actually began.

additional_sections.heading: FOUNDRY AND RESTORATION WORK (BY DISCIPLINE)
additional_sections.text:
Bronze Casting and Metallurgy
Cast and turned 40+ church and civic bells ranging from 2 cwt to 34 cwt, 2003-present, across three employers below.
Developed a revised copper-tin ratio for the foundry's small-bell range, reducing post-cast tuning corrections by an estimated one-third.
Personally supervised 60+ individual pours over the course of my career, including 4 large civic bells cast for municipal clock towers.
Tuning and Harmonic Analysis
Returned the 8-bell ring at a Grade I listed parish church (nominal note sequence restored to concert pitch after 140 years of drift).
Trained 3 apprentice tuners in five-tone harmonic analysis (hum, prime, tierce, quint, nominal).
Tower and Frame Engineering
Diagnosed and corrected a persistent "wolf" tone in a 6-bell ring that three previous tuning attempts by other foundries had failed to resolve.
Assessed and specified replacement headstocks and bearings for 12 towers.
Consulted on the structural loading assessment for a cathedral ring prior to a full rehang.
Advised a diocesan surveyor's office on 5 separate tower stability assessments following unrelated roof restoration work that had raised concerns about bell-frame loading.
Historical and Archival Research
Catalogued foundry marks and inscriptions on 60+ historic bells for a regional diocesan archive.
Contributing researcher, Church Bells of the Eastern Counties (Privately published survey, 2015).
Identified and correctly attributed a previously unmarked 17th-Century bell to a historic Whitechapel-area foundry lineage, based on alloy composition and inscription style, a finding accepted by the diocesan.
